transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well, it's mostly work stuff. I'm an electrician, and... I just keep going back over my jobs. Again and again. 

Just... checking things. Breakers, labels, torque marks... taking photos of them. Sometimes I even, uh, drive back to a site after I've already left. It's just making a simple install take way longer than it should. And, well, people are starting to notice. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to focus on something else?

Yeah... I guess so. Um... like, even after I know I checked a panel, or a disconnect... I'll just get this thought barging in. Just... thinking maybe I missed one loose neutral, or... left something that could start a fire. 

I try to just shake it off and focus on driving, but... it kind of just follows me all the way home.
Do you feel like you have to check things in a specific way or a certain number of times to feel okay about them?
Um... no, not really. I don't... I don't count them or anything like that. I just check until I'm sure it's fine, I guess. There's no specific number.
Do you feel like checking these things is necessary to prevent something bad from happening?
Um... I don't know. I guess? I'm not really sure. I just... I just want to make sure the job is done right. That's pretty much it.
Are you worried that if you don't check these things, something bad will happen, like someone getting hurt?
I mean... I guess nobody wants anyone to get hurt. But... I don't know if it's like a specific worry like that. I just... I just don't want to leave a mess behind.
Do you feel less anxious after you've checked everything?

I don't... I wouldn't really call it being anxious. I just... once I look it over, I know I'm finished. Then I can pack up my tools and move on to the next job. I don't really think about it past that.
Do you feel like checking these things is to prevent something bad from happening to someone else?
I mean... I think I just said that. No. It's not... I'm not picturing someone getting hurt or anything. I just want to know the work is right so I can go home. That's really all there is to it.
Do you think your checking is mostly to make sure you didn't make a mistake?
Yeah, I guess. I mean... nobody wants to do shoddy work. So... yeah. Just making sure it's done right.
Do you feel like your work has to be perfect, or is it more about not making any mistakes?

I don't really... I'm not sure what the difference is, to be honest. I guess they sound like the same thing to me. I just... I don't want there to be mistakes. I just want it done right so I can pack up.
Is it more important for you to make sure everything is perfect, or to make sure you haven't missed anything?
I don't know. Like I said, it just... it feels like the same thing. I just want it right. I don't know how else to explain it.
Do you think you would stop checking if someone else verified that your work was correct?
I don't know. Maybe. I mean... if they really knew what they were looking at, I guess. But... I'm the one who did the work, so it's on me. I'd probably still want to just... look at it myself.
Do you think you would feel okay with your work if someone else found a small mistake in it?
I don't know. I try not to let it get to that point, so... I couldn't really tell you. I just make sure it's right before I leave the site.
Do you think you would be satisfied with your work if it was good enough, but not perfect?
I don't think so. Good enough just... doesn't sit right with me. It needs to be done the way it's supposed to be done. Otherwise, what's the point?
Do you think the reason you check things multiple times is because you're afraid of what might happen if you make a mistake?

I suppose. It's just... even after I know I already checked a panel, or a disconnect... this thought just kind of barges in. Like maybe I missed one loose neutral, or... left something that could start a fire. I try to shake it off, but... it just follows me all the way home.
Do you think something very bad would happen if you didn't catch a mistake in your work?
I don't know. I mean... electricity isn't really something you want to mess around with. So... maybe. I just... I try not to think about it getting that far. That's why I check.
Is your main concern making sure everything is perfect, or is it about avoiding mistakes?
I guess... maybe a bit of both. I just want it done right. So nothing goes wrong.
Is your checking mostly to make sure everything is perfect or to avoid making a mistake that could have bad consequences?
I don't really know. Like I said, I just... I don't want a mistake to cause a problem. I don't really think about it having to be perfect. Just... safe, I guess.
Do you think something very bad would happen to someone else if you made a mistake in your work?
I don't really know. I guess it could. But I don't... I don't really sit around picturing people getting hurt or anything. I just try to do the job right so I don't have to find out.
Is your main reason for checking your work to prevent something bad from happening to the people who will be using the electrical systems you install?
I mean... I don't really think about the people using it. It's just... it's wires and panels. I just need to know the job is done right. That's all.
